name: Home organizing

crowd.buyer: Busy households and people moving or downsizing
not_yet: Don't buy bins before the sort and the measuring.
Don't haul, sell or store a client's things in your first month.
Don't take a home with blocked exits, pests or mold on your own.
crowd.note: Trust first: a free walk-through, the client's yes on every item, and photos only with a written okay.
crowd.basis: Scores, buyer, first $1 and not-yet lines: research/niches/organizing.json crowd_scores (our judgment). Best months: research/niches/organizing.json crowd (January is NAPO's GO Month, from a search result excerpt; spring and back to school are judgment).

safety: The client decides what stays and what goes, at their pace. Nothing leaves without their yes.
Price, minimum, supplies and any drop-off runs are agreed in writing before the work starts.
Never keep, buy or sell a client's things. Donations go where the client chooses, and the receipt goes to them.
Photos only with written permission, with nothing personal in frame, kept private and deleted on request.
Papers with account numbers are shredded only with the client's okay, and tax papers only after they check with their tax preparer.
Pests, mold, blocked exits or heavy furniture: don't take it on alone. Refer out, and leave heavy lifting to an insured moving company.

extra.title: Walk-through script (20 minutes, free)
lines: 1. Thanks for having me. Show me the space, and tell me what bothers you most.
2. What has to stay, and what are you happy to let go of? Nothing leaves without your yes.
3. Who uses this space, and what do you reach for most often?
4. May I measure the shelves, drawers and closet rods? Please don't buy bins yet.
5. Any papers, medicines or keepsakes I should know about? They stay where you can see them.
6. Is it okay to take before and after photos for your records? Nothing personal in frame, and nothing shared without your written okay.
7. For a first visit I'd plan 3 hours on the zones that bother you most. My founding price is {founding}. Want to set a day?

offer.name: Home organizing session
offer.basis: From research/niches/organizing.json: HomeAdvisor (most organizers charge $55 to $100 an hour), Thumbtack (average $65 an hour, most pay $60 to $75) and Fixr ($50 to $150 an hour, many with a 3-hour minimum), checked 2026-10-19. Supplies are extra, at cost.
includes: A free 20-minute walk-through before anything is booked
A written plan: zones, hours and what each zone needs
Sorting with you: keep, donate, recycle, trash or decide later
Setup and labels in your words, with supplies priced before anything is bought
steps: Free walk-through: you show me the space and what bothers you most.
You get a written plan with zones, hours and a supply list, and the price in writing.
We sort together, one zone at a time. Nothing leaves without your yes.
Supplies are bought after the sort and the measuring, at cost with receipts, then set up and labeled.
offer.promise: If I'm late, that hour is free. If you're not happy with how a zone is set up, tell me within a week and I'll come back and redo it at no charge.
offer.promise_note: I can't promise how a room will stay. I promise the work: the plan we agree on, your decisions followed, and every zone set up and labeled before I leave.
sheet_notes: Nothing is thrown out, donated or bought without your yes.
Photos only with your written okay, with nothing personal in frame.
What I see in your home stays private.
offer.footer: Billed per hour with a 3-hour minimum, or as a 6-hour room package.

partner_objections.label: They have rules
partner_objections.means: They have rules about posting or outside services.
partner_objections.answer: Thanks for explaining, and of course I'll follow your rules. Is there another way you share local services with residents or customers, like a newsletter or a resource list, that I could apply for?
partner_objections.next: Follow their rules exactly and ask about the approved way in.

partner_objections.label: They asked for a referral fee
partner_objections.means: They want to be paid for sending people your way.
partner_objections.answer: Thanks for asking straight out. I don't pay for referrals, so what I recommend to the people I help stays about them. I'm glad to point the people I help your way when it fits, with nothing owed either way.
partner_objections.next: Keep the partnership to cards and honest recommendations, both ways.

sources.says: I will not allow compensation from third parties to dictate my recommendations.
Make recommendations for products and services with my client's best interests in mind.

objections.label: It's more than clutter
objections.means: The home may have safety or sanitation problems beyond organizing.
objections.answer: Thank you for trusting me with that. When there are pests, mold or blocked doorways, the first step is the right help for safety, and I can share who to call. Once the space is safe, I'd be glad to help you set it up.
objections.next: Don't take it on alone. Refer out first. ICD's Clutter-Hoarding Scale is a guide for organizers, not a diagnosis.
objections.check: Know who you'd refer to (pest control, a mold specialist, a cleaning company) before you send this.

sources.says: An observational guideline for assessing safety, sanitation and usability in a home; not meant for clinical diagnosis.
Encourage my clients to seek the services of other professionals.

objections.label: Helping a parent downsize
objections.means: They're helping an older parent move to a smaller home.
objections.answer: That's a big move, and it goes at your parent's pace. I start with a free walk-through with them there, put the price in writing before any work, and nothing leaves without their yes. For the move itself, I work alongside a moving company you choose rather than hauling anything myself.
objections.next: Book the walk-through with the parent there, and give them the written estimate.

sources.says: Move managers help older adults and families downsize and relocate, outline the cost in a written estimate before payment, and work closely with a reputable local moving company.

objections.label: Will you post photos of my home?
objections.means: They want to know their home and things stay private.
objections.answer: Only with your written okay, and never with anything personal in frame. What I see in your home stays private: your papers, your things and your story.
objections.next: Put the photo and privacy terms in writing before the first visit.

sources.says: I will keep confidential all client information, and use proprietary client information only with the client's permission.

objections.label: Do I need to buy bins first?
objections.means: They're asking about supplies before the work.
objections.answer: Please don't buy anything yet. We sort first and measure, then buy only what fits, at cost with receipts, and we use what you already have first.
objections.next: Hold off on supplies until after the sort.

sources.says: The organizer's hourly rate does not usually include file cabinets, shelving or storage tools.
Make recommendations for products and services with my client's best interests in mind.

objections.label: Are you insured?

sources.says: A question to ask before hiring: are you fully insured for liability and workers' compensation?

objections.label: It costs too much
objections.means: The price is more than they expected.
objections.answer: That's fair. Two ways to make it work: start with the one zone that bothers you most in a single 3-hour visit, or book a 1-hour video check-in for a plan and a supply list you can follow yourself. A room package also costs a little less per hour.
objections.next: Hold your price. Offer the smaller start or the video check-in.

sources.says: Many organizers have an hourly minimum of 3 hours.
Buying home organization services in bulk typically decreases the overall cost per hour.

objections.label: I could do it myself

objections.means: They'd rather do the work themselves.
objections.answer: You can, and lots of people do. If it helps, a 1-hour video check-in gives you a zone-by-zone plan and a supply list to work from, and I'm a text away if you get stuck.

objections.label: Will you make me throw things away?

objections.label: I'm embarrassed by the mess

objections.answer: Thank you for telling me. There's no judging here, ever. We go at your pace, start wherever you like, and what I see stays private.
objections.next: Be warm and plain, then offer the walk-through.

win.title: Log the new client
win.description: A client said yes: logs the win in your Pipeline, writes the booking message, the prep message and the day-before reminder, and a printable first visit checklist.
win.booking: Hi {greet}, you're all set! Your first visit is {when}{where}. It's {deal}. We'll start with a quick walk through the space together, and nothing leaves your home without your yes.{pay}
win.prep: Before the visit: please hold off on buying bins or organizers. We'll measure first and pick supplies together, at cost with receipts. If you can, clear a spot to sort (a table or a bit of floor) and keep a few bags or boxes handy for donations.
win.reminder: Hi {greet}, see you {when}. Reply here if anything changes.
win.founding: Founding client: after the first visit, ask {greet} for honest feedback you may quote as a founding client, and ask in writing before you take or share any photo. Never ask for a review in exchange.

Walk-through: Walk the space together. Ask what bothers them most and what must stay.
Agree on the zones, the order and the hours for this visit.
Measure shelves, drawers and closet rods before anyone buys a bin.
Ask, in writing, about before and after photos. No yes, no photos.
Confirm the price, the minimum and how supplies are paid for, in writing.
Every visit: Sort into keep, donate, recycle, trash and decide later. The client makes every call.
Work one zone at a time, and finish it before starting the next.
Keep papers and mail where the client can see them. Shred only with their okay.
Label containers in the client's own words.
After: Walk the finished zones together and show where everything lives.
Drop donations only where the client chose, and pass on the receipt.
Send the invoice with the supply receipts attached.
Book the next zone or the next room.
